test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 12 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.**

(**No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, that**) one of my long-suffering 17 readers was into action.

options.text: No sooner had the ink dry on last week's column, than
No sooner did the ink dried on last week's column, than
No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, than

solution:
The correct answer is **"No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, than."**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"no sooner...than"** is a correct and commonly used way to express that one event happened immediately after another.
 
• The original sentence is incorrect because it uses **"that"** instead of **"than"** after **"no sooner had."**
 
 
• **Example: ***No sooner had I started mowing the lawn than it started raining.*
 
 
 
• The correct verb tense to use with this phrase is **"had" + past participle (e.g. had dried).**
 
• So, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**Correct sentence:** ***No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, than**__ one of my long-suffering 17 readers was into action.*
